newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods--Gulf gasoline firms as shorts cover.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods--Gulf gasoline firms as shorts cover.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast spot gasoline differentials lifted in afternoon talk amid shortcovering some players were saying was linked to a emerging squeeze play on the NYMEX, traders said.

But others said the buying was just simple shortcovering, perhaps an early move ahead of a Colonial Pipeline scheduling deadline on Tuesday. In New York Harbor, MTBE continued to be the driving force behind gasoline's strength.
On the NYMEX, gasoline led the upward move in products, with August gasoline gaining 0.81 cent to finish at 64.84 cents a gallon and August heating oil up 0.15 cent to end at 54.14 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF
Refiner buying and Tuesday's scheduling deadline for prompt (front 22nd cycle) M1-conventional unleaded gasoline pushed up differentials in moderate Monday afternoon activity.
Differentials for prompt M1 barrels firmed a cent, with deals heard done at 0.50 cent over the print. Offers were pegged at 0.85 cent over in late trade.
"There was a lot of short covering out there this afternoon," said a cash trader, noting the upcoming Colonial Pipeline scheduling deadline late Tuesday on the M1-grade.
"Most of the push was on the front end," the trader added.
Any month barrels were traded at 3.00 cents below the screen.
Prompt 93-octane premium gasoline firmed more than a half cent to 6.25/6.75 cents on tight supply.
The distillate were a tad weaker, with the prompt ranged 2.75/2.50 cents below the Merc. Any month barrels were done at 2.40 cents below the screen.
54-grade jet fuel for front 22nd traded at 0.35 cent over the screen, even with last week.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Gasoline differentials remained firm in New York riding a continuing wave of strength in MTBE markets.
"I don't think it'll get much higher, but it'll stay at these levels for a while," said one industry consultant fairly expressing the prevailing view in MTBE and gasoline markets.

There were a few bearish voices among traders, but for the moment they were in the minority, with the question of when additional cargoes of both finished gasoline and MTBE might arrive one of the big disagreements between bulls and bears.

For the moment the "A2" regular northern-grade reformulated held its value, with prompt barrels still offered at about 2.25 cents over, and barrels for delivery by the beginning of next month heard offered at 2.00 cents over.

The "V2" and "D2" 93-octane conventional and reformulated northern blends also held their strength, with prompt barrels of both grades offered as high as 7.25 and 11.50 cents over August NYMEX unleaded.
MIDCO
Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials were stable in slow trade on Monday amid a trickle of position squaring ahead of the close of the month.
Group Three unleaded gasoline remained 0.75/0.50 cents below the screen, with a few deals done.
Chicago market material for prompt barrels was about 0.25/0.50 cents above the screen but gasoline for August 1 to 10 delivery was pegged 3.00 cents over ther screen.
Players said supply tightened this week but more material is seen for next week on the Williams Pipeline system.
"We have lower days of supply and futures came off but we do have lots of stuff coming next week in the system," said a trader.
The distillate market also weakened, with Group Three down to 2.00/2.25 cents over the print.
-- New York Oil Desk +1 212 859 1620
